newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha rises in reaction to strong crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha rises in reaction to strong crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha rose on Friday in reaction to strong crude prices, but upward momentum was weak compared with crude, traders said on Friday.
"Naphtha prices have been high recently, therefore room to move upwards may be limited compared to crude," a trader said.
"Prices may rise after trading in London starts," he said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half May was assessed at $231.00/232.00, up from Wednesday levels of $230.00/232.00, and for second-half May at $228.00/229.00, up from $226.50/228.50.
On Thursday, first-half May was traded at $232.00 and second-half May at $225.00, traders said.
Inter-month spreads were barely changed, with first-half May/first-half June sandwiched between $6.00, and second-half May/second-half June at about $4.50/5.00, traders said.
Traders said sentiment was firm, supported by demand from South Korean and Japanese petrochemical product makers.

Compared to last year, turnarounds at Japanese ethylene plants this year are slightly less in number and more spread out, a trader said. A Japanese petrochemical maker said overall turnarounds may be fewer than last year, but that ongoing production cuts by some makers would weigh on demand.
